import re

line = "Hopper, Grace  09:45  ADD R1 R2"
m = re.search(r"(\w+), (\w+)\s+(\d{2}):(\d{2})", line)

print("group(0):", m.group(0))
print("group(1):", m.group(1), "| group(2):", m.group(2))
print("groups():", m.groups())
print("span(3): ", m.span(3), "->", line[m.start(3):m.end(3)])

named = re.search(r"(?P<last>\w+), (?P<first>\w+)\s+(?P<hh>\d{2}):(?P<mm>\d{2})", line)
print("groupdict():", named.groupdict())

plain = re.search(r"(?:\w+), (\w+)", line)
print("with (?:...), group(1) is:", plain.group(1))

print("findall, 0 groups:", re.findall(r"R\d", line))
print("findall, 1 group: ", re.findall(r"R(\d)", line))
print("findall, 2 groups:", re.findall(r"(R)(\d)", line))
description: This example extracts fields from a line and shows how capture groups shape regex results.

steps.description: The pattern captures a last name, first name, hour, and minute from line.
group(0) returns the whole match. Numbered groups return individual captures, and span(3) locates the hour in the original line.

steps.answer: It uses the names last, first, hh, and mm from the named capture groups.
steps.question: What keys will groupdict() use for the named match?

steps.description: Named groups turn the captures into a dictionary. The noncapturing group at line 14 matches the last name without adding a numbered capture.
findall returns whole matches with no groups, captured strings with one group, and tuples when the pattern has two groups.
The two-group pattern returns one tuple for each register name.
